pages.text: "Mom, the pumpkins are piled like a mountain!" Coco walked through the market, holding Mom's apron hem tightly. Every tent was full of chestnuts, apples, and pumpkins. Mom looked down. "Hold my apron tight. Lose Mom? Stay right there!"
Coco stopped by a yellow pumpkin. "Wow! It's bigger than me!" Coco quietly let go of the apron and rushed over. While Coco tapped the pumpkin, Mom's footsteps grew farther away.
When Coco finished tapping and looked up, Mom's apron was gone. Everywhere were strange legs, legs, legs. Coco's eyebrows drooped, and their mouth turned down.
Then Mom's voice rang in Coco's ears. "Lose Mom? Stay right there!" Coco stopped on that very spot. One big breath. Whew. Coco pulled the scarf knot tight with both paws. "It's okay. I can do this."
Mrs. Magpie, who saw everything from the roof, flew above the market. A red dot stood still in the middle of the crowd. "That red dot is Coco!" She flew down.
She hopped down in front of Coco. "Have you lost Mom?" Coco spoke clearly. "Yes. So I stayed right here." "Well done. Lose Mom? Stay right there! I'll look for her from above."
Mrs. Magpie flew up and circled the market. "There! Bakery Mom with flour on her arms!" she called loudly. Coco waited with feet planted. Seeing her wings above made it less scary.
Far away between the tents, Mom came running with the bread basket. "Coco!" Coco left the spot, ran to her, and grabbed her apron with both paws. Mom patted Coco's back, leaving white flour marks.
Mom placed Coco's paw firmly on her apron hem again. "One, stay right there! Two, don't run around! Three, tell a grown-up you know, 'I'm Coco from the bakery!'" Coco held the apron even tighter.
Mom lifted Coco into her arms. Mrs. Magpie waved her wings above. "If we lose each other and you stay there, I'll find you." Coco hugged Mom's neck. "Lose Mom? Stay right there!"
